subject: POC trial: model selection and evaluation plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Diego Ramos <diego@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: POC trial: model selection and evaluation plan

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC/trial based on our discovery:

Summary of ask
- Primary use case: clinical triage assistant for inbound patient messages (short clinical summaries, intent classification, suggested triage)
- Volume: ~1,200 messages/day initially; peak ~5k/day
- Multilingual: English + Spanish required now, French possibly later
- Data sensitivity: PHI may be present; customer needs private deployment option or strong data controls

Proposed POC scope (2-4 weeks)
1) Success criteria (we suggested):
   - Accuracy: intent classification F1 >= 0.85 on a 500-sample test set
   - Summarization quality: ROUGE-L / human score target (will define rubric)
   - Latency: 95th percentile < 450 ms for 1-2k qps using Redwood Dedicated profile
   - Failure mode: robust fallback to a smaller model with deterministic outputs for safety-critical paths
2) Evaluation plan:
   - You provide a de-identified sample set (we can onboard via secure S3 or VPC link)
   - We run model candidates on the set, produce metrics and sample outputs, and run a short manual review (10-15 examples) with your clinical SME
3) Model candidates suggested for trial:
   - Primary: Llama 3 13B (quantized + Redwood optimizations) - good mix of accuracy and cost
   - Multilingual/fallback: Mistral 7B or Llama 3 7B as a fast, lower-cost fallback (Spanish-tested)
   - If strict PHI policy: run in Private deployment with customer-managed KMS
4) Ownership & timeline:
   - Redwood POC lead: Marissa Cole (cc'd) - onboarding, infra, metrics
   - Customer POC lead: Elena / Diego - dataset, SME reviews
   - Target kickoff: Week of Nov 16; initial results by Nov 30

Action items / asks from Acme Health by EOD next Tue (Nov 12):
- Confirm target success criteria and any additional safety checkpoints
- Provide a de-identified 200-500 sample extract (or confirm you want Redwood to generate a synthetic set first)
- Confirm whether Private deployment is required or Hosted+Dedicared acceptable

I've attached a starter success-criteria template (POC-success-criteria.xlsx) and our network requirements (network-config.pdf) for the Private path. Marissa will follow up to coordinate infra access and the evaluation rubric.

Thanks - looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: POC-success-criteria.xlsx, network-config.pdf

From: Elena Park <elena@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Ramos <diego@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-11T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection and evaluation plan

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. This looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- Multilingual: Spanish support is a hard requirement for MVP (approx 30% of traffic). French is low priority for now.
- PHI: We can share de-identified samples for the first pass. If results look promising, we will need the Private deployment option for production.
- Success criteria: the F1 >= 0.85 for intent sounds reasonable; for summaries our clinicians will rate on a 1-5 trust scale and we'll target an average >= 4.0.
- Timeline: Nov 16 kickoff works. We'll deliver the 300-sample de-identified set by Nov 13 EOD.

Questions:
1) For Spanish, do you expect equivalent performance from Llama 3 13B out of the box or do we need to add Spanish-specific fine-tuning / prompt engineering?
2) For the fallback model, we'd prefer a model with known deterministic behavior for the safety-critical routing - is Mistral 7B typically more deterministic than Llama 3 7B?

I've CC'd Diego who will be our technical contact for infra and procurement.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park | Director of Clinical Ops
Acme Health
elena@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@acmehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Diego Ramos <diego@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T11:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection and evaluation plan

Thanks Elena - great signal on requirements. I'll own the POC on the Redwood side and coordinate infra/setup. A couple of practical notes and proposed adjustments:

1) Spanish support: Llama 3 13B generally performs well on Spanish out of the box, but for clinical nuance we recommend a small-stage instruction-tuning pass or a few-shot prompt template tuned to your clinical phrasing. We can include a short prompt-engineering iteration in week 1 of the POC.

2) Fallback behavior: Jordan, tagging you for confirmation on determinism and fallback orchestration. Our usual approach: primary model for general responses, deterministic smaller model for safety-critical yes/no decisions (we can use a beam-limited quantized 7B with temperature=0 and strict output schema).

3) Timeline / tasks:
   - Nov 13: Acme delivers 300 de-identified samples (Elena)
   - Nov 16: Kickoff; Redwood creates test harness, S3 ingestion, evaluation scripts (Marissa)
   - Nov 16-20: Run candidates on dataset, generate metrics + sample outputs; include Spanish-specific checks
   - Nov 23-25: Clinical SME review and rubric scoring (Acme)
   - Nov 30: Deliver final POC report and recommended production configuration

4) Access / security:
   - Diego: please confirm whether you want us to use a Hosted/Private hybrid during the POC (we can process de-id data on Hosted infra, but recommend Private if PHI is present).

Action items:
- Elena/Diego: confirm delivery of samples by Nov 13 and Preferred deployment for POC (Hosted+Dedicated vs Private).
- Jordan: please attach the evaluation harness and the deterministic-fallback config we typically use.

Ben and I will prepare the evaluation rubric and populate the attached POC-success-criteria.xlsx with your thresholds.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@acmehealth.com>, Diego Ramos <diego@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection and evaluation plan

Marissa / team -

Attaching the evaluation harness and fallback config (see attachments stub). Quick technical notes:

- Evaluation harness: includes dataset ingestion, tokenization parity checks, metric scripts (intent F1, ROUGE-L, length/distribution checks), and a Spanish-focused BLEU/ROUGE check. We'll run on Dedicated capacity with telemetry enabled.
- Primary model: Llama 3 13B (quantized int8 + Redwood kernel optimizations). Expect top-tier quality across English/Spanish with minimal prompt tuning.
- Fallback: Mistral 7B quantized with temperature=0 and output-schema enforcement for safety-critical decisions. Mistral 7B tends to be faster and more consistent for short deterministic outputs; Llama 3 7B is an alternative but may require stronger prompt constraints for determinism.
- Data handling: if Acme wants Private POC, we'll provide a VPC peering guide; otherwise we'll use a temporary secure S3 with customer-managed KMS.

I'll drop the harness in the Drive folder and send a HubSpot update after kickoff.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake | Lead SRE, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
